pl-l4d50c2-d1e115.summary: Asks why the darkness enveloping the wicked in Gehenna is called outer.

pl-l4d50c2-d1e118.summary: Answers: because then the wicked will be wholly outside bodily and spiritual light, God; now, though they suffer darkness in (sentence continues).
claims: The damned will be wholly outside God's light.

pl-l4d50c2-d1e121.summary: Completes: blindness of mind, they are not wholly outside God's light nor deprived of bodily light.
claims: In this life no one is wholly outside God's light.

pl-l4d50c2-d1e125.summary: Quotes Augustine: God's wrath will be at the judgment and is here in blindness of mind when the wicked are given up to a reprobate sense; there will be outer darkness, since sinners will be wholly outside God; what is it to be wholly outside God but to be in supreme blindness, since God dwells in light inaccessible? This darkness begins here in the sinner, cut off from God's inner light, but not wholly while in this life.
claims: Outer darkness is supreme blindness, complete separation from God.
It begins in this life but is not complete here.

pl-l4d50c2-d1e143.summary: Draws out that the sinner is said to suffer outer darkness there and not here, since there he will be wholly cut off from God's light.

pl-l4d50c2-d1e146.summary: Asks how that separation is to be understood: because they will not see God by sight? But no one here sees God by sight. By the unlikeness sin makes? But many here are far from God by grave sins. Because they hate God and wish he did not exist? But many here hate God. What then is that distance?

pl-l4d50c2-d1e152.summary: Answers that outer darkness can be understood as a malignity of hatred and will growing in the minds of the reprobate, and a forgetting of God, since they will be so affected and disturbed by inner and outer torments that they scarcely, rarely, or never recall the mind to think of God, as those crushed by great weight are stunned and think only of where pain is felt. But in this life no one is so wicked as to be wholly cut off from thought of God, not having lost the desire for happiness and a certain love of good natural to the rational creature.
claims: Outer darkness is growing hatred and forgetting of God.
In this life the natural desire for happiness and good remains.

pl-l4d50c2-d1e155.summary: Adds that Augustine says the reprobate will suffer that outer and deepest darkness after the judgment, contrasting the rich man in hell who saw Abraham and Lazarus and confessed his evils and asked that his brothers be warned, which is read as before the judgment; after the judgment the impious will be in deeper darkness, seeing no light of God to confess to.
claims: After the judgment the damned see no light of God.

pl-l4d50c2.summary: Asks why the darkness of hell is called outer: because the wicked will be wholly outside bodily and spiritual light, God, whereas now, though blind of mind, they are not wholly outside God's light. Augustine: then sinners will be wholly outside God, in supreme blindness; this darkness begins here but is not complete in this life. How this separation is to be understood, since no one sees God by sight now, sin already distances many, and many already hate him: the outer darkness is a malignity of hatred and will growing in the reprobate and a forgetting of God, so overwhelmed by torment that they scarcely or never think of God; while in this life no one is so wicked as to lose all thought of God, the desire for happiness and natural love of good. After the judgment the impious will be in deeper darkness than the rich man, who still saw Abraham and confessed.
claims: Outer darkness is total separation from God's light.
It consists in growing hatred and forgetting of God amid torment.
In this life no one loses all thought of God or natural love of good.
After the judgment the darkness of the damned deepens.
